results.reason: The memo quotes Supply Agreement §14.2, including the more-than-50% ownership trigger, the consent requirement and the 30-day termination right. It notes that the 100% stock sale triggers it, that Schedule 4.4 says 'None', and that the §7.2(c) condition only covers consents listed on Schedule 4.4.
Issue G identifies the asymmetric assignment rights under §16.1. It explains the risk that the sole-source supplier could be transferred to a competitor or less reliable party.

Issue A states the 120-day notice requirement before Dec 31, 2026, puts the deadline at Sept 2, 2026, and notes it passed before the Sept 21 SPA date. It treats the extension and Extension Pricing as at risk or lost.
Issue C quotes Side Letter §2 limiting Fundamental Reps to 4.1 and 4.2. It explains that §11.11 precedence makes this control, so 4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the deductible and the $8.45M cap.

Issue D identifies Delaware law and Chancery under the Side Letter against New York law and forum under SPA §11.8 and §11.9. It explains that precedence lets the Side Letter control, splitting indemnity disputes from other disputes.
The memo states the cap is $8,450,000, or 10% of the Purchase Price.
The memo states that §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority, ahead of the SPA.
The memo is addressed to [Partner]. Each issue is a distinct item listing the documents and sections, why it matters, and a recommended action, often with proposed language.
Issues are ordered by significance, with an opening section and a summary table of items requiring a client call before responding to the other side.
The memo states the deadline has passed and does not say the option remains exercisable.
The memo correctly states that 4.3 and 4.12 are now capped and that the Side Letter controls; it makes neither of the prohibited statements.
